_about: Rites of passage (src/rites.py): gates locked by keys their keepers carry (the key crumbles when used; the gate is warded against picks, bashes and spells; the zone reset locks it again), and toll-keepers who carry you across for a fare (talk, pay, or give them gold). Loaded at world load after world/population.

necropolis-key.short_desc: a bone key carved like a finger
necropolis-key.description: A long key carved from a single finger bone, yellowed and polished by a guardian's grip. It is cold, and it fits only the door of the ruined temple.

oracle-key.description: A curved gold key shaped like a lion's claw, still warm from the Sphinx's throat. It opens the Oracle's chamber.

altar-key.description: A small key of rose-gold, worked with doves and myrtle. It opens the way to Aphrodite's altar.

hades-key.description: A heavy key of black iron, rough as if it had been forged in a hurry by a smith who feared it. It opens the gates of Hades.

white-key.description: A key the colour of bleached driftwood. It opens the white gate.

gray-key.description: A key the colour of cold ash. It opens the gray gate.

black-key.description: A key so dark it seems to swallow the light around it. It opens the black gate to Tartarus.

ember-key.description: A key of glowing red metal, hot enough to make the palm sweat. It opens the fiery door.

rime-key.description: A key cut from blue ice that never melts. It opens the icy door.

mist-key.description: A grey key that is solid only for now, its edges curling like fog. It opens the misty door.

z51-key.description: A key spun from hardened spider silk, black and faintly sticky. It opens the Grand Temple of Lloth.

z53-key.description: A heavy gold key with a scarab for its head. It opens the way down into the tomb of Ramses.

z63-key.description: A key cut from a spider's black chitin, sharp at the edges. It opens the lair of Arachnos.

z90-key.description: A rusty key with a handle of yellow bone. It opens the Bog Witch's hut.

z426-key.description: A key as long as a forearm, forged for a giant's hand. It opens the giant's lair.

z447-key.description: A heavy key black with soot. It opens the way to the caves below Mahn-Tor.

z470-key.description: A long key topped with a little crown. It opens the royal chambers.

z480-key.description: A plain iron cellar key, worn smooth. It opens the basement.

z491-key.description: A crude, heavy key hammered out by goblin smiths. It opens the Guarded Hall.

z499-key.description: A small bronze key engraved with a star chart. It opens Phaeton's secret study.

z503-key.description: A dwarf-forged key cut with runes of oath and stone. It opens the gate to the stronghold.

z507-key.description: A key of dark red metal, warm as skin. It opens the Vampire Lord's den.

z512-key.description: A key of black iron with a crown of little bones for its head. It opens the way to the throne room.

z522-key.description: A key of blue glacier ice that numbs the hand. It opens the frost giant's hall.

z64-key.description: A key of cloudy glass that shows a different dream each time you look into it. It opens Rand's bedroom.

z62-key.description: A crude key on a thong of hide. It opens the way to Elstar.

gates.why: Island of the Dead: the Necropolis Warden keeps the temple door
the Sphinx keeps the Oracle's chamber
the Siren keeps Aphrodite's altar
Cerberus keeps the gates of Hades
the white gate
the gray gate
the black gate to Tartarus
Alecto keeps the fiery door
Megaera keeps the icy door
Tisiphone keeps the misty door, before Hades' throne

keeper.long_desc: The Temple Warden of Lloth bars the temple doors, a silk key at her throat.
keeper.description: A drow priestess in robes of black spider-silk, her face painted with the eight-legged sign. The Spider Queen's favour hangs on her like a perfume, and she guards the temple door against all who are not of the faith.

gates.why: Drow City: the Temple Warden keeps the Grand Temple of Lloth

keeper.long_desc: The Tomb Guardian stands over the sealed stair, a gold scarab key bound to its wrist.
keeper.description: A tall mummy in bandages stiff with resin and gold leaf, a priest of the dead king buried alive to keep his tomb. A scarab-headed key is bound to its wrist with a strip of linen.

gates.why: Great Pyramid: the Tomb Guardian keeps Ramses' tomb

keeper.long_desc: The Brood Warden crouches before the lair, a key of black chitin caught in its silk.
keeper.description: An enormous grey spider, scarred and patient, that has fed on adventurers for a hundred years. A key of black chitin hangs in the silk across its back.

gates.why: Arachnos: the Brood Warden keeps the Spider Queen's lair

keeper.long_desc: Old Snapjaw, the Bog Witch's familiar, lies before her door with a key in its teeth.
keeper.description: A huge old alligator, grey with age and moss, that the Bog Witch keeps as her doorkeeper. It holds a bone-handled key in its jaws and does not let go of it while it lives.

gates.why: Haunted Swamp: Old Snapjaw keeps the Witch's hut

keeper.long_desc: The Warden of the Lair stands before the giant's door, an iron key at its hip.

gates.why: Troglodyte Mines: the Warden keeps Hrungar's lair

keeper.long_desc: The Keep's Gatewarden stands before the cave gate, a soot-black key on a chain.

gates.why: Mahn-Tor Keep: the Gatewarden keeps the way to the caves

keeper.long_desc: The Royal Doorwarden stands before the royal chambers, a crowned key at its belt.

gates.why: Castle of Ostragoth: the Royal Doorwarden keeps the royal chambers

keeper.long_desc: The Thrall Steward guards the cellar door, the cellar key on a ribbon round its neck.

gates.why: Salem's Lot: the Thrall Steward keeps the basement

keeper.long_desc: The Hall Sergeant stands before the Guarded Hall, a crude iron key at his belt.

gates.why: Morvoct: the Hall Sergeant keeps the warlord's hall

keeper.long_desc: The Bronze Warden stands before the study door, a bronze key set in its palm.

gates.why: Phaeton's Academy: the Bronze Warden keeps the secret study

keeper.long_desc: The Gatestone stands before the stronghold gate, a rune key sunk in its brow.

gates.why: Durmandel I: the Gatestone keeps the stronghold

keeper.long_desc: The Blood Herald waits before the den, a blood-red key at his throat.

gates.why: Lost Crypt II: the Blood Herald keeps the Vampire Lord's den

keeper.long_desc: The Throne Warden of Morkai bars the way to the throne room, a bone-crowned key at its belt.

gates.why: Morkai: the Throne Warden keeps the way to Gorbash

keeper.long_desc: The Frost Herald drifts before the great hall, a key of glacier ice in its hand.

gates.why: The Winterlands: the Frost Herald keeps Hrimgar's hall
Rand's Tower: the Demon of Decay keeps the master bedroom

keeper.long_desc: The Orc Huntmaster guards the tunnel door, a key on a hide thong round his neck.

gates.why: The Orc Enclave: the Huntmaster keeps the tunnel to Elstar

bars.name: River Styx
bars.say: The Styx slides past, black and deep. No one swims it and no boat but Charon's crosses it. He waits at the wharf for his coin.

journey: The black boat slides out from the wharf. Charon leans on his pole without a word.
Pale faces turn beneath the water as you pass, mouths opening on names you do not know.
The far bank rises out of the dark: a landing of black stone, and beyond it, gates.

say.greet: Charon turns his hooded head toward you and holds out a bony hand. 'One coin for the crossing,' he rasps. 'The dead pay it under the tongue. You, living one, may pay it in your hand.'
say.pay: Pay the ferryman one gold coin.
say.ask: What waits on the other side?
say.lore: 'The gates of Hades, and the dog that keeps them. The judges. The white gate, the gray and the black, and below them Tartarus.' His coal eyes do not blink. 'Every gate has its keeper, and every keeper its key. Take the key and the gate is yours. One coin.'
say.bye: Charon says nothing. The boat rocks at the wharf.
say.paid: Charon closes his fingers on the coin. He steps down into the black boat and nods you aboard.
say.broke: Charon's hand stays out. 'No coin, no crossing,' he rasps.
say.arrive: The boat bumps against the far landing. Charon pushes off into the dark without looking back.
say.short: Charon looks at what you offer and does not take it. 'One coin.'

bars.name: River Styx
bars.say: The Styx slides past, black and deep. The hollow oarsman sits in his boat at the landing, waiting for a coin.

journey: The grey boat slides back across the black water. The oarsman rows without a sound.
Behind you the gates of Hades shrink into the dark.

say.greet: The hollow oarsman lifts the face that is not there. 'Back to the living? One coin.'
say.pay: Pay the oarsman one gold coin.
say.ask: Why do you row the living back?
say.lore: 'Charon carries the dead one way. The living are my lord's mistake, and I correct it.' His voice is the creak of an oar. 'One coin.'
say.paid: The oarsman takes the coin and dips his oars.
say.broke: 'One coin,' says the oarsman, and waits.
say.arrive: The boat grates against the wharf. The oarsman is already rowing away.

make.long_desc: An old river bargeman waits by his flat barge at the edge of the Quay.
make.description: He is brown and creased as a walnut, with forearms like ropes from a life of poling barges against the current. For a few coins he will take you up the river into the mountains, where no raft could fight the rapids.

journey: The barge pushes off from the Quay into the brown current.
The city falls behind. Steep banks rise on either side, and the old man leans on his pole against the rapids.
The river narrows into a tunnel cut through the mountain, and the roar of water fills the dark.

say.greet: The old bargeman squints up at you. 'Upriver? Into the mountain? Five gold and I'll pole you there, rapids and all.'
say.lore: 'East, up through the levee and under the mountain. There's a landing in the tunnel, and past it the desert. No raft gets up those rapids. My barge does.'
say.paid: The bargeman pockets the coins and waves you aboard.
say.broke: 'Five gold,' says the bargeman. 'I don't pole for free.'
say.arrive: The barge bumps against a rock landing inside the mountain tunnel. 'Mind the step,' says the bargeman.

make.long_desc: A river bargewoman sits on her moored barge at the rock landing, mending a net.
make.description: She is broad and weatherbeaten, with a pipe clamped in her teeth and a long pole across her knees. She takes travellers down the river to Garathorm's Quay, which is easy going with the current behind you.

journey: The barge slides out of the tunnel and down the rapids, the current doing all the work.
The banks open out, and the walls and roofs of Garathorm rise ahead.

say.greet: The bargewoman takes the pipe from her mouth. 'Down to Garathorm? Five gold. It's a quick trip with the current.'
say.lore: 'Safe enough in a barge. In a raft you'd be matchwood on the rocks.'
say.bye: She goes back to her net.
say.paid: She takes the coins and casts off.
say.arrive: The barge noses in against the Quay. 'Here you are. Garathorm.'
